fields.Title: Swan Lake
fields.Caption: A performance at His Majesty's Theatre, Brisbane, 1953
fields.Creator: Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov
fields.Notes: Tchaikovsky's score failed in Julius Reisinger's Moscow staging of 1877; this revival, made after the composer's death, is the version danced today.
fields.Captions: A performance at His Majesty's Theatre, Brisbane, 1953
fields.Clue: One ballerina dances both the enchanted Odette and her double, Odile, whose thirty-two fouettés in Act III are the test of the role.

fields.Title: The Nutcracker
fields.Caption: A dancer as the Nutcracker
fields.Creator: Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov
fields.Notes: Tchaikovsky's ballet, from Alexandre Dumas's version of E. T. A. Hoffmann's tale; Ivanov made the dances to Petipa's plan.
fields.Gallery captions: Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, its composer, in 1888 | A Rubicon Dance Company production
fields.Clue: Its “Dance of the Sugar Plum Fairy” introduced the celesta, an instrument the composer kept secret so no rival would use it first.

fields.Title: The Rite of Spring
fields.Caption: Nicholas Roerich's design for the 1913 production
fields.Creator: Vaslav Nijinsky
fields.Notes: Igor Stravinsky's score, with its irregular metres; Nicholas Roerich designed the production.
fields.Captions: Nicholas Roerich's design for the 1913 production
fields.Clue: A chosen maiden dances herself to death in a pagan ritual, to stamping, turned-in choreography that caused a riot at the premiere.

fields.Title: Giselle
fields.Caption: Carlotta Grisi in the title role
fields.Creator: Jean Coralli and Jules Perrot
fields.Notes: Adolphe Adam's score; the definitive Romantic ballet, whose white-tulle corps gave the era the term ballet blanc.
fields.Captions: Carlotta Grisi in the title role
fields.Gallery captions: Carlotta Grisi, the first Giselle, 1841 | A set design for the Ballets Russes production at the Paris Opéra, 1910
fields.Clue: In Act II, the Wilis, ghosts of women who died before their wedding days, try to dance a faithless nobleman to death.

fields.Title: Romeo and Juliet
fields.Caption: Galina Ulanova and Yuri Zhdanov in Lavrovsky's production
fields.Creator: Leonid Lavrovsky
fields.Notes: Prokofiev's score was first staged complete in Brno in 1938; this Kirov production, with Galina Ulanova, is the one that entered the repertory.
fields.Captions: Galina Ulanova and Yuri Zhdanov in Lavrovsky's production
fields.Gallery captions: A 2010 production at the Royal Swedish Opera
fields.Clue: Its composer first wrote a happy ending, reasoning that the dead cannot dance, and the Soviet authorities rejected the score.

fields.Title: The Sleeping Beauty
fields.Caption: Léon Bakst's costume design for the Ballets Russes' The Sleeping Princess, London, 1921
fields.Creator: Marius Petipa
fields.Notes: The fullest collaboration between Petipa and Tchaikovsky, whom he gave bar-by-bar instructions.
fields.Captions: Margot Fonteyn and Robert Helpmann, Sadler's Wells Ballet
fields.Clue: Its “Rose Adagio,” in which four suitors each partner the princess on her sixteenth birthday, is among the hardest tests of a ballerina's balance.

fields.Title: Coppélia
fields.Caption: Wilma Haydee Giglio dancing Swanilda at the Prix de Lausanne, 2010
fields.Alternate: Coppélia, ou La Fille aux yeux d'émail
fields.Creator: Arthur Saint-Léon
fields.Notes: Léo Delibes's score, after E. T. A. Hoffmann's The Sandman.
fields.Gallery captions: A 2010 production
fields.Clue: A comic ballet in which Swanilda impersonates the mechanical doll her fiancé has fallen for.

fields.Title: The Firebird
fields.Caption: Léon Bakst's costume design for the Firebird, 1910
fields.Creator: Michel Fokine
fields.Notes: Stravinsky's first Ballets Russes commission made him famous, after Anatoly Lyadov missed the deadline.
fields.Captions: Léon Bakst's costume design for the Firebird, 1910
fields.Gallery captions: Léon Bakst's costume design for the Firebird, 1910
fields.Clue: Prince Ivan spares a magical creature, who later helps him destroy the ogre Koschei by breaking the egg that holds his soul.

fields.Title: Appalachian Spring
fields.Caption: Martha Graham, who choreographed it and danced the Bride, about 1940
fields.Creator: Martha Graham
fields.Notes: Aaron Copland wrote it for Graham, who took the title from a Hart Crane poem after the score was finished; Isamu Noguchi designed the set.
fields.Captions: Isamu Noguchi's set for the 1944 premiere
fields.Clue: A ballet of a young pioneer couple, whose score closes with variations on the Shaker tune “Simple Gifts.”

fields.Title: Petrushka
fields.Caption: Alexandre Benois's design for the 1911 premiere
fields.Creator: Michel Fokine
fields.Notes: Stravinsky's score; its signature chord stacks C major against F-sharp major.
fields.Captions: Vaslav Nijinsky in the title role
fields.Gallery captions: Fairground Booths in Tula, 1873: the kind of Shrovetide fair where the ballet is set | Igor Stravinsky with Nijinsky, in costume as Petrushka
fields.Clue: A puppet given a soul at a Shrovetide fair loves a ballerina and is killed by a Moor.

fields.Title: La Bayadère
fields.Caption: The Kingdom of the Shades in Natalia Makarova's staging, Polish National Ballet
fields.Creator: Marius Petipa
fields.Notes: Ludwig Minkus's score; the temple dancer Nikiya dies from a snake hidden in a basket of flowers.
fields.Captions: The Kingdom of the Shades in Petipa's final revival, Mariinsky Theatre
fields.Gallery captions: Lev Ivanov as the warrior Solor in the original production, 1877 | Lev Ivanov as Solor in the original production, 1877
fields.Clue: In the Kingdom of the Shades, the corps descends a ramp one dancer at a time, each repeating the same arabesque.

fields.Title: Don Quixote
fields.Caption: The pas de deux, Compañía Nacional de Danza
fields.Creator: Marius Petipa
fields.Notes: Ludwig Minkus's score; Petipa took only the Kitri and Basilio episode from Cervantes, and its Act III pas de deux is a gala staple.
fields.Captions: The pas de deux, Compañía Nacional de Danza
fields.Gallery captions: A production in Venezuela, 2013
fields.Clue: A ballet built on the romance of the innkeeper's daughter Kitri and the barber Basilio, in which the title knight barely dances.

fields.Title: Revelations
fields.Caption: The “Wade in the Water” section
fields.Creator: Alvin Ailey
fields.Notes: Alvin Ailey's signature work; “Wade in the Water” is its best-known section.
fields.Gallery captions: At the Avignon Festival, 1977
fields.Clue: A modern dance set to spirituals and gospel, drawn from its choreographer's memories of Texas churches, that closes with “Rocka My Soul.”

fields.Title: Rodeo
fields.Creator: Agnes de Mille
fields.Venue: Metropolitan Opera House, New York City
fields.Notes: Aaron Copland's score; de Mille danced the Cowgirl herself.
fields.Clue: A cowgirl competes with the ranch hands to win the head wrangler, to a score whose “Hoe-Down” became one of the most familiar pieces of American music.

fields.Title: The Dying Swan
fields.Caption: Anna Pavlova in costume for The Dying Swan
fields.Creator: Michel Fokine
fields.Notes: Set to “The Swan” from Saint-Saëns's The Carnival of the Animals; Pavlova is said to have asked for its costume on her deathbed.
fields.Captions: Anna Pavlova in costume for The Dying Swan
fields.Clue: A four-minute solo made for Anna Pavlova, who danced it some four thousand times.

fields.Title: Parade
fields.Caption: Pablo Picasso's costumes for the Managers, on exhibition
fields.Creator: Léonide Massine
fields.Notes: Erik Satie's score includes a typewriter; Jean Cocteau wrote the scenario.
fields.Captions: Pablo Picasso's costume design for the 1917 premiere
fields.Gallery captions: Erik Satie, its composer, painted by Ramon Casas | Léonide Massine, its choreographer
fields.Clue: Pablo Picasso designed its Cubist costumes, and Guillaume Apollinaire coined the word “surrealism” in its program note.

fields.Title: Jewels
fields.Caption: Alina Cojocaru and Rupert Pennefather
fields.Creator: George Balanchine
fields.Venue: New York State Theater, New York City
fields.Notes: Often called the first full-length abstract ballet.
fields.Clue: Three plotless acts: Emeralds to Fauré, Rubies to Stravinsky, and Diamonds to Tchaikovsky.

fields.Title: The Three-Cornered Hat
fields.Caption: Manuel de Falla, its composer
fields.Creator: Léonide Massine
fields.Notes: Manuel de Falla's score; Massine studied Spanish dancers for its farruca, and it premiered in London in 1919.
fields.Clue: A miller's wife outwits a lecherous magistrate, in a Spanish ballet designed by Pablo Picasso.

fields.Title: Le Spectre de la rose
fields.Caption: Vaslav Nijinsky and Tamara Karsavina in the first performance, 1911
fields.Creator: Michel Fokine
fields.Notes: Set to Weber's Invitation to the Dance, orchestrated by Berlioz; Vaslav Nijinsky's exit through the window was the most famous jump of his career.
fields.Captions: Vaslav Nijinsky and Tamara Karsavina in the first performance, 1911
fields.Gallery captions: Nijinsky in the rose petal costume
fields.Clue: A girl home from her first ball dreams that the flower she wore comes to life to dance with her, and leaves with a famous leap through the window.

fields.Title: The Red Detachment of Women
fields.Caption: A scene from the ballet
fields.Notes: Premiered in 1964 and made one of the Eight Model Operas of the Cultural Revolution; it was performed for Richard Nixon in 1972.
fields.Clue: A peasant girl escapes a tyrannical landlord and joins a unit of female soldiers on Hainan Island.

fields.Title: Agon
fields.Caption: Carolina Ballet in performance
fields.Creator: George Balanchine
fields.Notes: Igor Stravinsky's score.
fields.Clue: A plotless ballet for twelve dancers built on seventeenth-century French court dances, to a partly twelve-tone score.

fields.Title: Apollo
fields.Caption: Ballets Russes dancers in Apollon musagète
fields.Creator: George Balanchine
fields.Notes: Igor Stravinsky's score; Balanchine called it the turning point of his life, when he learned that gestures could be eliminated.
fields.Gallery captions: Falco Kapuste as Apollo
fields.Clue: A young god is visited by the Muses of poetry, mime, and dance, and chooses Terpsichore.

fields.Title: Fancy Free
fields.Caption: A performance of the ballet
fields.Creator: Jerome Robbins
fields.Venue: Metropolitan Opera House, New York City
fields.Notes: Leonard Bernstein's score; Robbins's first ballet grew into the musical On the Town.
fields.Gallery captions: Kansas City Ballet in Fancy Free
fields.Clue: Three sailors on shore leave compete for two girls in a bar.

fields.Title: Martha Graham
fields.Caption: Photographed by Nickolas Muray
fields.Notes: She ran her company for sixty-five years, with sets by Isamu Noguchi; Appalachian Spring, Night Journey, and Lamentation are hers.
fields.Gallery captions: Martha Graham and Bertram Ross as Clytemnestra and Orestes
fields.Clue: Choreographer who built a modern-dance technique on contraction and release.

fields.Title: George Balanchine
fields.Caption: At Schiphol Airport, 1965
fields.Notes: Agon, Apollo, Serenade, and Jewels are his; he told dancers, “See the music, hear the dance.”
fields.Gallery captions: Balanchine in the 1920s
fields.Clue: Co-founder of New York City Ballet, who made plotless ballet the American style.

fields.Title: Marius Petipa
fields.Caption: Signed portrait photograph
fields.Notes: The Sleeping Beauty, Don Quixote, La Bayadère, and Acts I and III of the 1895 Swan Lake are his.
fields.Gallery captions: Petipa in Saint Petersburg, c. 1855 | Act I of Petipa's final revival of The Pharaoh's Daughter, Mariinsky Theatre, 1898
fields.Clue: Ballet master at the Imperial Theatres in Saint Petersburg for over thirty years, and the author of most of the classical repertory.

fields.Title: Vaslav Nijinsky
fields.Caption: As Vayou in Le Talisman
fields.Notes: He choreographed The Rite of Spring and Afternoon of a Faun; schizophrenia ended his career in his twenties.
fields.Gallery captions: Nijinsky in Scheherazade | Nijinsky as Armide's slave in Michel Fokine's Le Pavillon d'Armide
fields.Clue: The Ballets Russes star famed for seeming to hang in the air at the top of his leaps.

fields.Title: Alvin Ailey
fields.Caption: Photographed by Carl Van Vechten, 1955
fields.Notes: Revelations, set to spirituals, is his signature work.
fields.Gallery captions: Alvin Ailey, photographed by Carl Van Vechten, 1955 | Revelations, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, 2011
fields.Clue: Choreographer who founded his company in 1958 to make a place for Black dancers in modern dance.

fields.Title: Bob Fosse
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph for Pal Joey, 1963
fields.Notes: Chicago, Cabaret, Pippin, and Sweet Charity are his; in 1973 he won the Oscar, the Emmy, and the Tony.
fields.Clue: Choreographer of turned-in knees, rolled shoulders, bowler hats, and white gloves.

fields.Title: Jerome Robbins
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph, c. 1968
fields.Notes: Fancy Free and Dances at a Gathering for ballet, West Side Story and Fiddler on the Roof for Broadway; he named names to the House Un-American Activities Committee.
fields.Gallery captions: Jerome Robbins, about 1968
fields.Clue: Choreographer who worked at the top of ballet and of Broadway at the same time.

fields.Title: Anna Pavlova
fields.Caption: In The Dying Swan, Berlin
fields.Notes: She toured farther than any dancer of her generation, and made The Dying Swan her own.
fields.Gallery captions: Anna Pavlova in 1905
fields.Clue: Ballerina for whom a meringue dessert is named.

fields.Title: Merce Cunningham
fields.Caption: Photographed by Fernand Michaud
fields.Notes: He used chance procedures, such as tossing coins, to order movement.
fields.Clue: Choreographer who made dance and music independently with John Cage, so that the two met only in performance.

fields.Title: Agnes de Mille
fields.Caption: Photographed by Lynn Gilbert
fields.Notes: She also made Rodeo and danced its Cowgirl; she was Cecil B. DeMille's niece.
fields.Captions: As the Priggish Virgin in Three Virgins and a Devil, 1941
fields.Gallery captions: In her apartment, 1978
fields.Clue: Choreographer whose dream ballet in Oklahoma! made dance carry the plot of a Broadway show.

fields.Title: Michel Fokine
fields.Caption: As Harlequin
fields.Notes: The Firebird, Petrushka, The Dying Swan, and Le Spectre de la rose are his.
fields.Gallery captions: Fokine as Lucien d'Hervilly in Petipa's Paquita, 1905 | Fokine as the Spirit of the Rose in Le Spectre de la rose, 1914
fields.Clue: Choreographer who argued that steps should serve the drama rather than display, and made the Ballets Russes' first Paris seasons.

fields.Title: Twyla Tharp
fields.Caption: At the National Medal of Arts presentation, 2004
fields.Notes: Push Comes to Shove for Mikhail Baryshnikov, and Movin' Out to Billy Joel.
fields.Captions: At the National Medal of Arts presentation, 2004
fields.Gallery captions: Tharp in 1981
fields.Clue: Choreographer who crossed ballet with popular music, and made a Broadway show from Billy Joel's songs.

fields.Title: Misty Copeland
fields.Caption: At a Broadway opening night, 2016
fields.Notes: She came to ballet at thirteen, late for a professional, at a Boys and Girls Club in San Pedro.
fields.Gallery captions: Copeland in Coppélia, 2014
fields.Clue: The first Black woman promoted to principal dancer at American Ballet Theatre, in 2015.

fields.Title: Sergei Diaghilev
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1916
fields.Notes: He commissioned Igor Stravinsky, Claude Debussy, Erik Satie, Pablo Picasso, and Henri Matisse.
fields.Gallery captions: Sergei Diaghilev by Valentin Serov, 1904 | Léon Bakst, Portrait of Sergei Diaghilev with His Nanny, 1905
fields.Clue: Impresario who founded the Ballets Russes, though he neither danced nor choreographed.

fields.Title: Mikhail Baryshnikov
fields.Caption: At the Latvian parliament, 2017
fields.Notes: He went on to lead American Ballet Theatre.
fields.Gallery captions: With Patricia McBride in Buenos Aires, 1979 | With Liza Minnelli in Baryshnikov on Broadway, 1980
fields.Clue: Dancer who defected from the Soviet Union in Toronto in 1974.

fields.Title: Frederick Ashton
fields.Caption: Robert Heindel's portrait of Ashton taking a curtain call
fields.Notes: La Fille mal gardée, Symphonic Variations, and Cinderella are his.
fields.Clue: Choreographer who made the English style at Sadler's Wells and the Royal Ballet: lyrical, understated, and built on épaulement.

fields.Title: Rudolf Nureyev
fields.Caption: After his defection from the Soviet Union, 1961
fields.Notes: He formed a long partnership with Margot Fonteyn, nineteen years his senior.
fields.Captions: After his defection from the Soviet Union, 1961
fields.Gallery captions: With Margot Fonteyn and Fred Astaire on The Hollywood Palace, 1965
fields.Clue: Dancer who defected at Le Bourget airport in 1961.

fields.Title: Katherine Dunham
fields.Caption: Photographed for the New York World-Telegram, 1956
fields.Notes: She refused to perform for segregated audiences.
fields.Captions: Photographed for the New York World-Telegram, 1956
fields.Gallery captions: Dunham in Tropical Revue, Martin Beck Theatre, 1943 | By Carl Van Vechten, 1940
fields.Clue: Anthropologist and choreographer who studied Caribbean dance and built it into a technique.

fields.Title: Isadora Duncan
fields.Caption: Dover Street Studios, London, c. 1910
fields.Notes: She was killed when her scarf caught in the wheel of a car in Nice.
fields.Gallery captions: Dancing barefoot on her American tour, 1915–18; photograph by Arnold Genthe | Anna, Lisa, and Margot, three of her pupils, the “Isadorables”
fields.Clue: Dancer who performed barefoot in a Greek tunic, against the strictures of ballet.

fields.Title: Paul Taylor
fields.Caption: Photographed by Carl Van Vechten, 1960
fields.Notes: One of the last of the Graham generation; he founded his own company in 1954.
fields.Gallery captions: Dancing, 1960
fields.Clue: Choreographer from Martha Graham's company whose Esplanade is built from walking, running, and falling.

fields.Title: Maria Tallchief
fields.Caption: Dance Magazine, April 1961
fields.Notes: George Balanchine, her husband, made the Sugar Plum Fairy and the Firebird on her.
fields.Gallery captions: Tallchief with Erik Bruhn in 1961 | As the Sugar Plum Fairy, with Nicholas Magallanes, in Balanchine's The Nutcracker, 1954
fields.Clue: Osage ballerina who was the first American prima ballerina.

fields.Title: Margot Fonteyn
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph, 1960s
fields.Notes: Her partner was Rudolf Nureyev, nineteen years her junior; Frederick Ashton made many roles on her.
fields.Gallery captions: With Robert Helpmann in Façade, 1936 | With Helpmann in The Sleeping Beauty, Sadler's Wells Ballet, 1950
fields.Clue: Royal Ballet ballerina whose late partnership with a Soviet defector extended her career by fifteen years.

fields.Title: Léonide Massine
fields.Caption: Portrait drawing
fields.Notes: He choreographed Parade and The Three-Cornered Hat, and appears in the film The Red Shoes.
fields.Clue: Choreographer who succeeded Nijinsky at the Ballets Russes.

fields.Title: Fred Astaire
fields.Caption: Publicity portrait for You'll Never Get Rich, 1941
fields.Notes: He danced ten films with Ginger Rogers, and began in vaudeville with his sister, Adele.
fields.Captions: Publicity portrait for You'll Never Get Rich, 1941
fields.Gallery captions: With his sister Adele, 1906 | With Ginger Rogers in Top Hat, 1935
fields.Clue: Dancer who insisted his dances be filmed in full figure and in long takes, so the camera never cut away.

fields.Title: Gene Kelly
fields.Caption: Publicity portrait
fields.Notes: Singin' in the Rain and An American in Paris are his best known; in Anchors Aweigh he dances with Jerry the cartoon mouse.
fields.Gallery captions: Poster for Singin' in the Rain, 1952 | Poster for An American in Paris, 1951
fields.Clue: Dancer who brought an athletic, working-man style to film musicals.

fields.Title: Ballets Russes
fields.Caption: Jean Cocteau's poster for the 1911 season: Nijinsky in Le Spectre de la rose
fields.Creator: Sergei Diaghilev
fields.Notes: Sergei Diaghilev founded it in 1909; The Firebird, Petrushka, The Rite of Spring, and Parade were its premieres.
fields.Captions: Jean Cocteau's poster for the 1911 season: Nijinsky in Le Spectre de la rose
fields.Gallery captions: Léon Bakst's set design for L'Après-midi d'un faune, 1912 | August Macke, Russian Ballet I, 1912
fields.Clue: Company that made modern ballet, commissioning Stravinsky's first three ballets, and never once performed in Russia.

fields.Title: The Royal Ballet
fields.Caption: A ballerina statue facing the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden, the company's home
fields.Creator: Ninette de Valois
fields.Notes: Frederick Ashton and Kenneth MacMillan built its repertory, and Margot Fonteyn was its star.
fields.Captions: A ballerina statue facing the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden, the company's home
fields.Gallery captions: Blue plaque for Ninette de Valois, its founder
fields.Clue: Company founded by Ninette de Valois as the Vic-Wells Ballet.

fields.Title: Bolshoi Ballet
fields.Caption: At the reopening gala of the Bolshoi Theatre, 2011
fields.Notes: Its rival is the Mariinsky (formerly Kirov) in Saint Petersburg, known for classical restraint.
fields.Captions: At the reopening gala of the Bolshoi Theatre, 2011
fields.Gallery captions: Anna Tikhomirova performing in Delhi
fields.Clue: The larger and more athletic of the two great Russian ballet companies, in Moscow.

fields.Title: Joffrey Ballet
fields.Caption: The Auditorium Building, Chicago, the company's home theatre from 2003 to 2020
fields.Creator: Robert Joffrey
fields.Notes: Robert Joffrey founded it in New York in 1956; it moved to Chicago in 1995.
fields.Clue: Company known for reviving lost works, including a reconstruction of Nijinsky's original Rite of Spring.

fields.Title: Pina Bausch
fields.Caption: At the Avignon Festival
fields.Notes: Café Müller and her Rite of Spring, danced on peat, are her most revived works.
fields.Gallery captions: Frühlingsopfer (The Rite of Spring, 1975), performed in 2009 | Nelken (1982), danced on a stage covered in carnations
fields.Clue: Choreographer who defined Tanztheater, in which dancers speak and repeat actions to exhaustion on stages covered in soil, water, or carnations.

fields.Title: Café Müller
fields.Caption: The chair-strewn stage of Café Müller
fields.Creator: Pina Bausch
fields.Notes: Pina Bausch danced in it herself; it opens Pedro Almodóvar's film Talk to Her.
fields.Clue: Dancers move with their eyes closed through a stage full of chairs while another performer clears the furniture from their path.

fields.Title: Merce Cunningham Dance Company
fields.Caption: Ocean, Carnival Center, Miami, 2007
fields.Creator: Merce Cunningham
fields.Notes: It gave its last performance at the Park Avenue Armory in 2011.
fields.Gallery captions: Merce Cunningham, its founder
fields.Clue: Dance company that disbanded two years after its founder's death, by his own instruction.

fields.Title: William Forsythe
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2012
fields.Notes: In the Middle, Somewhat Elevated is the piece most companies dance.
fields.Clue: American choreographer at Ballett Frankfurt who took classical technique apart from the inside.

fields.Title: Bill T. Jones
fields.Caption: At the Lincoln Presidential Library
fields.Notes: He founded his company with his partner, Arnie Zane, and choreographed Spring Awakening and Fela! on Broadway.
fields.Clue: Choreographer whose Still/Here, made from workshops with terminally ill people, set off a critical fight over “victim art.”

fields.Title: Mark Morris
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2006
fields.Notes: He founded the Mark Morris Dance Group in 1980, and directed dance at the Théâtre Royal de la Monnaie in Brussels.
fields.Clue: Musically exact, often comic choreographer whose largest work sets Handel's L'Allegro, il Penseroso ed il Moderato.

fields.Title: Michael Bennett
fields.Notes: That musical was A Chorus Line; he also staged Dreamgirls.
fields.Clue: Director and choreographer who built a Broadway musical from taped sessions with dancers about their own lives.

fields.Title: Busby Berkeley
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1933
fields.Notes: 42nd Street and Footlight Parade are his; the effects are less choreography than camera design.
fields.Gallery captions: “By a Waterfall” from Footlight Parade, 1933 | Carmen Miranda in his The Gang's All Here, 1943
fields.Clue: Choreographer who filmed chorus girls from overhead in kaleidoscopic geometric patterns.

fields.Title: Loie Fuller
fields.Caption: Engraved portrait from the Album Mariani, c. 1900
fields.Notes: She held patents on the lighting and the apparatus, and starred at the Folies Bergère.
fields.Captions: Engraved portrait from the Album Mariani, c. 1900
fields.Gallery captions: By Frederick Glasier, 1902
fields.Clue: Dancer who swirled metres of silk on extended wands under coloured electric light.

fields.Title: Ruth St. Denis
fields.Caption: In a Japanese-inspired costume
fields.Notes: The school was Denishawn; her solos drew on Indian and Egyptian subjects.
fields.Gallery captions: In one of her Indian-inspired solos | Ruth St. Denis in Egypta, 1910 | With the Denishawn dancers in Ishtar of the Seven Gates
fields.Clue: Dancer who founded, with Ted Shawn, the school that trained Martha Graham, Doris Humphrey, and Charles Weidman.

fields.Title: Ted Shawn
fields.Caption: By Arthur F. Kales, c. 1918
fields.Notes: He co-founded Denishawn with his wife, Ruth St. Denis.
fields.Gallery captions: With his wife, Ruth St. Denis, 1916 | With Ruth St. Denis in an Egyptian ballet
fields.Clue: Choreographer who founded Jacob's Pillow, and an all-male company to argue that dance was not unmanly.

fields.Title: Doris Humphrey
fields.Caption: In Shadowland magazine, September 1922
fields.Notes: Her rival system was Martha Graham's contraction and release; José Limón was her protégé.
fields.Clue: Choreographer who built a technique on fall and recovery, the body's negotiation with gravity.

fields.Title: José Limón
fields.Caption: In the Federal Theatre Project's Candide, c. 1936
fields.Notes: Born in Mexico, he trained with Doris Humphrey, who became his company's artistic director.
fields.Captions: In the Federal Theatre Project's Candide, c. 1936
fields.Clue: Choreographer whose The Moor's Pavane compresses Othello into four dancers and twenty minutes.

fields.Title: Lester Horton
fields.Caption: Bella Lewitzky and Sondra Orans in Horton's Warsaw Ghetto, 1949
fields.Notes: Alvin Ailey trained with him, and his technique is still taught.
fields.Captions: Bella Lewitzky and Sondra Orans in Horton's Warsaw Ghetto, 1949
fields.Clue: Choreographer who ran one of the first racially integrated dance companies in the United States, in Los Angeles.

fields.Title: Yvonne Rainer
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2014
fields.Notes: Trio A is the central work of postmodern dance; she was a founder of the Judson Dance Theater.
fields.Clue: Choreographer whose No Manifesto rejected spectacle, virtuosity, and the seduction of the spectator.

fields.Title: Anna Halprin
fields.Caption: At the University of San Francisco
fields.Notes: Yvonne Rainer, Trisha Brown, and Simone Forti studied with her.
fields.Captions: At the University of San Francisco
fields.Clue: Choreographer who worked outdoors on a dance deck in the Marin hills, and made dance from ordinary tasks.

fields.Title: Trisha Brown
fields.Notes: Set and Reset, designed by Robert Rauschenberg, is her best-known stage work.
fields.Gallery captions: Her company in performance
fields.Clue: Choreographer who sent dancers walking down the sides of buildings in harnesses.

fields.Title: Matthew Bourne
fields.Caption: Backstage at Edward Scissorhands, Melbourne, 2006
fields.Notes: It became the longest-running full-length ballet in the West End and on Broadway.
fields.Clue: Choreographer whose Swan Lake replaced the female corps with male swans.

fields.Title: Crystal Pite
fields.Caption: Photographed in June 2010
fields.Notes: Betroffenheit and Emergence are hers; her company is Kidd Pivot, in Vancouver.
fields.Gallery captions: Louise Lecavalier in Pite's Lone Epic, 2007
fields.Clue: Canadian choreographer whose large ensembles move as one body, like a swarm.

fields.Title: Akram Khan
fields.Caption: At Jerwood Space, London, 2010
fields.Notes: DESH and Zero Degrees are his; he choreographed part of the opening ceremony of the London 2012 Olympics.
fields.Gallery captions: Akram Khan Company in Vertical Road, Leicester, 2010
fields.Clue: Choreographer trained in both kathak and contemporary dance, who works across the two.

fields.Title: Wayne McGregor
fields.Caption: At the Venice Biennale Danza, 2025
fields.Notes: Chroma and Woolf Works are his.
fields.Clue: Royal Ballet choreographer who works with cognitive scientists on how dancers think.

fields.Title: La Sylphide
fields.Caption: Lucile Grahn, the Sylph of Bournonville's 1836 production
fields.Creator: August Bournonville
fields.Notes: Herman Løvenskiold's score; the oldest ballet still danced as it was made, after Filippo Taglioni's Paris original of 1832.
fields.Captions: Lucile Grahn, the Sylph of Bournonville's 1836 production
fields.Gallery captions: Carlotta Grisi in La Sylphide | Marie Taglioni as the Sylph in Filippo Taglioni's original, Paris, 1832
fields.Clue: A Scottish farmer abandons his bride on their wedding day to chase a winged spirit into the forest, where a witch's poisoned scarf kills her.

fields.Title: Les Sylphides
fields.Caption: Valentin Serov's poster of Anna Pavlova for the 1909 Saison Russe
fields.Creator: Michel Fokine
fields.Notes: Set to Chopin, and first staged in Saint Petersburg as Chopiniana; an early step toward abstract ballet.
fields.Captions: Valentin Serov's poster of Anna Pavlova for the 1909 Saison Russe
fields.Gallery captions: A performance in Baku, 2014 | Alexandre Benois's set design, 1909
fields.Clue: A plotless reverie of a poet among spirits in the moonlight, to orchestrated piano pieces.

fields.Title: Le Corsaire
fields.Caption: Charles-Antoine Cambon's set design for Act III, Scene 1
fields.Creator: Joseph Mazilier
fields.Notes: Adolphe Adam's score, after Lord Byron's poem.
fields.Captions: Charles-Antoine Cambon's set design for Act III, Scene 1
fields.Gallery captions: Vadim Muntagirov and Alina Cojocaru as Conrad and Medora, English National Ballet, 2013
fields.Clue: A ballet that survives mostly as its pas de deux for Medora and the slave Ali, a standard male showpiece.

fields.Title: The Green Table
fields.Creator: Kurt Jooss
fields.Notes: Fritz Cohen's score for two pianos; it won the first international choreography competition, in Paris in 1932.
fields.Clue: An anti-war dance framed by masked diplomats haggling at a conference while Death takes everyone.

fields.Title: Afternoon of a Faun
fields.Caption: Nijinsky as the Faun, photographed by Adolph de Meyer, 1912
fields.Creator: Vaslav Nijinsky
fields.Notes: Set to Debussy's prelude after Stéphane Mallarmé's poem; Nijinsky danced the lead himself.
fields.Captions: Nijinsky as the Faun, photographed by Adolph de Meyer, 1912
fields.Gallery captions: The final pose, with the nymph's scarf
fields.Clue: A ballet whose flat, frieze-like choreography and erotic closing gesture caused a scandal in the Paris press.

fields.Title: Daphnis et Chloé
fields.Caption: Léon Bakst's set design for Act I, 1912
fields.Creator: Michel Fokine
fields.Notes: Maurice Ravel's score, which he called a choreographic symphony, after Longus's pastoral romance.
fields.Captions: Léon Bakst's set design for Act I, 1912
fields.Gallery captions: Michel Fokine, its choreographer | Pirates in the Ballets Russes premiere, 1912
fields.Clue: A Ballets Russes commission now more often heard as orchestral suites, the second of which opens with a sunrise.

fields.Title: Serenade
fields.Caption: Kansas City Ballet in the opening tableau, 2021
fields.Creator: George Balanchine
fields.Notes: Set to Tchaikovsky's string serenade; it opens with seventeen women in blue raising their arms against the light.
fields.Captions: Kansas City Ballet in the opening tableau, 2021
fields.Gallery captions: Kaleena Burks and Kelsey Hellebuyck of Kansas City Ballet in Serenade
fields.Clue: Its choreographer's first ballet made in America, on students, keeping a dancer's fall and another's late arrival from rehearsal.

fields.Title: The Four Temperaments
fields.Caption: Kansas City Ballet, 2015
fields.Creator: George Balanchine
fields.Venue: Central High School of Needle Trades, New York City
fields.Notes: Balanchine commissioned the score from Paul Hindemith himself, and paid five hundred dollars for it.
fields.Gallery captions: Angelina Sansone and Liang Fu, Kansas City Ballet
fields.Clue: A ballet in variations named for the humours: melancholic, sanguine, phlegmatic, and choleric.

fields.Title: Dances at a Gathering
fields.Caption: The Royal Ballet at the curtain call
fields.Creator: Jerome Robbins
fields.Venue: New York State Theater, New York City
fields.Notes: Made for New York City Ballet in 1969.
fields.Captions: The Royal Ballet at the curtain call
fields.Clue: An hour-long plotless ballet for ten dancers, to Chopin played on stage, that returned its choreographer to ballet from Broadway.

fields.Title: Romeo and Juliet
fields.Caption: Miyako Yoshida as Juliet, curtain call at the Royal Ballet
fields.Creator: Kenneth MacMillan
fields.Notes: The Royal Ballet's signature full-length work, to Prokofiev's score.
fields.Captions: Miyako Yoshida as Juliet, curtain call at the Royal Ballet
fields.Clue: The leads were made on Lynn Seymour and Christopher Gable, but management gave the premiere to Margot Fonteyn and Rudolf Nureyev.

fields.Title: Manon
fields.Caption: Curtain call at the Prague premiere of L'Histoire de Manon, 2025
fields.Creator: Kenneth MacMillan
fields.Notes: Leighton Lucas arranged the Massenet music.
fields.Captions: Curtain call at the Prague premiere of L'Histoire de Manon, 2025
fields.Clue: A ballet after the Abbé Prévost, set to music arranged from everything its composer wrote except his opera on the same story.

fields.Title: Mayerling
fields.Caption: Alina Cojocaru, Johan Kobborg, and Laura Morera, Royal Ballet
fields.Creator: Kenneth MacMillan
fields.Notes: Set to Franz Liszt, arranged by John Lanchbery.
fields.Captions: Alina Cojocaru, Johan Kobborg, and Laura Morera, Royal Ballet
fields.Clue: The murder-suicide of the Habsburg crown prince Rudolf, one of the most demanding male roles in the repertory.

fields.Title: Onegin
fields.Caption: Roberta Marquez as Tatiana and Thiago Soares in the title role
fields.Creator: John Cranko
fields.Notes: Made for the Stuttgart Ballet in 1965; Tatiana tearing up a letter ends it.
fields.Captions: Roberta Marquez as Tatiana and Thiago Soares in the title role
fields.Clue: A ballet after Pushkin, built from music by Tchaikovsky that is not from his opera on the same story.

fields.Title: Kenneth MacMillan
fields.Caption: Photographed late in life
fields.Notes: Romeo and Juliet, Manon, Mayerling, and his own Rite of Spring are his.
fields.Gallery captions: English Heritage blue plaque at his home in Wandsworth, London
fields.Clue: Choreographer who brought psychological darkness and adult subject matter into British ballet.

fields.Title: John Cranko
fields.Caption: Eva Zippel's drawing of Cranko, 1965
fields.Notes: Onegin and The Taming of the Shrew are his; he died on a flight home from America in 1973.
fields.Clue: South African choreographer who built the Stuttgart Ballet into a company of international standing.

fields.Title: Judson Dance Theater
fields.Caption: Judson Memorial Church, New York
fields.Venue: Judson Memorial Church, New York City
fields.Notes: Yvonne Rainer, Trisha Brown, Steve Paxton, and Lucinda Childs all passed through.
fields.Clue: A few dozen performances in a Greenwich Village church, from 1962 to 1964, that began postmodern dance.

fields.Title: Louis Armstrong
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1947
fields.Notes: “West End Blues” opens with the most studied cadenza in jazz.
fields.Gallery captions: With the Fletcher Henderson Orchestra, 1925
fields.Clue: Trumpeter whose Hot Five and Hot Seven recordings made jazz a soloist's art.

fields.Title: Miles Davis
fields.Caption: Photographed by Tom Palumbo
fields.Notes: Birth of the Cool, Kind of Blue, the second great quintet, and Bitches Brew.
fields.Gallery captions: Tommy Potter, Charlie Parker, Max Roach, Miles Davis, and Duke Jordan in August 1947 | At the piano with Howard McGhee, Joe Albany, and Brick Fleagle, 1947
fields.Clue: Trumpeter who led five revolutions in jazz, from cool through modal to jazz-rock.

fields.Title: Duke Ellington
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph
fields.Notes: “Mood Indigo” and the suite Black, Brown and Beige are his; his theme, “Take the ‘A’ Train,” was written by Billy Strayhorn.
fields.Gallery captions: Directing his orchestra at the Hurricane Ballroom, New York, 1943 | At a radio studio, 1954
fields.Clue: Bandleader who wrote for the particular players in his orchestra rather than for instruments.

fields.Title: John Coltrane
fields.Caption: Arriving at Schiphol Airport, 1963
fields.Notes: Giant Steps, A Love Supreme, and Ascension; he died at forty.
fields.Clue: Saxophonist who moved from sheets of sound to modal devotion and then to free playing.

fields.Title: Dizzy Gillespie
fields.Caption: At the Famous Door, New York, c. 1947
fields.Notes: He invented bebop with Charlie Parker, and brought Afro-Cuban rhythm into jazz with “Manteca.”
fields.Captions: At the Famous Door, New York, c. 1947
fields.Gallery captions: At the Famous Door, New York, about 1946, photographed by William P. Gottlieb | Gillespie (left) with John Lewis, Cecil Payne, Miles Davis, and Ray Brown, 1946–48
fields.Clue: Trumpeter who played a horn with its bell bent upward.

fields.Title: Dave Brubeck
fields.Caption: Arriving at Schiphol Airport, 1964
fields.Notes: “Take Five,” in five-four, was written by his saxophonist, Paul Desmond.
fields.Gallery captions: The quartet in 1967
fields.Clue: Pianist whose quartet's Time Out put jazz in unusual metres.

fields.Title: Ella Fitzgerald
fields.Caption: Photographed by Carl Van Vechten, 1940
fields.Notes: Called the First Lady of Song, she recorded the Song Books for Verve.
fields.Gallery captions: With Dizzy Gillespie and Ray Brown, New York, 1947
fields.Clue: The finest scat singer in jazz, whose Song Book series set the repertory of American standards.

fields.Title: Charlie Parker
fields.Caption: At the Three Deuces, New York, 1947
fields.Notes: “Ko-Ko,” “Ornithology,” and “Now's the Time” are his; the coroner guessed his age at over fifty.
fields.Captions: At the Three Deuces, New York, 1947
fields.Gallery captions: His King Super 20 alto saxophone, now at the Smithsonian | With Tommy Potter, Max Roach, Miles Davis, and Duke Jordan at the Three Deuces, New York, 1947
fields.Clue: Alto saxophonist who invented bebop with Dizzy Gillespie, and died at thirty-four.

fields.Title: Charles Mingus
fields.Caption: In Lower Manhattan on the Bicentennial, July 4, 1976
fields.Notes: Mingus Ah Um and The Black Saint and the Sinner Lady are his; his autobiography is Beneath the Underdog.
fields.Captions: In Lower Manhattan on the Bicentennial, July 4, 1976
fields.Gallery captions: Playing the double bass, 1976
fields.Clue: Bassist and composer whose Jazz Workshop turned collective improvisation into composition.

fields.Title: Ornette Coleman
fields.Caption: Playing alto saxophone in concert
fields.Notes: The Shape of Jazz to Come and Free Jazz; he played a plastic saxophone.
fields.Captions: At the Enjoy Jazz Festival, Heidelberg, 2008
fields.Gallery captions: Playing violin with Prime Time, 1978
fields.Clue: Saxophonist whose album abandoning fixed chord changes gave free jazz its name.

fields.Title: Thelonious Monk
fields.Caption: At Minton's Playhouse, New York, c. 1947
fields.Notes: He was the house pianist at Minton's Playhouse, where bebop was born.
fields.Captions: At Minton's Playhouse, New York, c. 1947
fields.Gallery captions: Thelonious Monk (Amsterdam, 1961) | Thelonious Monk, 1964
fields.Clue: Pianist of angular, dissonant lines full of silence, whose “'Round Midnight” is the most recorded standard by a jazz composer.

fields.Title: Herbie Hancock
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2023
fields.Notes: He played in Miles Davis's second great quintet, and wrote “Watermelon Man” and “Cantaloupe Island.”
fields.Gallery captions: Hancock in 2023
fields.Clue: Pianist whose Head Hunters was the first jazz album to go platinum.

fields.Title: Bill Evans
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph, 1961
fields.Notes: He played on Kind of Blue; his trio with Scott LaFaro recorded Sunday at the Village Vanguard.
fields.Clue: Pianist who brought impressionist harmony to the piano trio, and made it a conversation.

fields.Title: Scott Joplin
fields.Caption: Portrait photograph
fields.Notes: “Maple Leaf Rag” and “The Entertainer,” which returned to fame in the film The Sting.
fields.Gallery captions: Joplin in 1907
fields.Clue: The King of Ragtime, who could not get his opera Treemonisha staged in his lifetime.

fields.Title: Nina Simone
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1969
fields.Notes: Classically trained, she was refused by the Curtis Institute; she was born Eunice Waymon.
fields.Gallery captions: Nina Simone in 1965
fields.Clue: Singer and pianist who wrote “Mississippi Goddam” after the Birmingham church bombing.

fields.Title: Billie Holiday
fields.Caption: With her dog Mister, New York, 1947
fields.Notes: Called Lady Day, a name Lester Young gave her.
fields.Captions: With her dog Mister, New York, 1947
fields.Clue: Singer who phrased behind the beat, and made the anti-lynching song “Strange Fruit” her closing number.

fields.Title: Benny Goodman
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph, 1942
fields.Notes: The King of Swing; his trio and quartet, with Teddy Wilson and Lionel Hampton, were among the first racially integrated groups to perform in public.
fields.Gallery captions: Goodman's swing fans in Oakland, California, in 1940
fields.Clue: Clarinetist whose 1938 Carnegie Hall concert made jazz respectable.

fields.Title: Stan Getz
fields.Caption: At Kastrup Airport, Copenhagen
fields.Notes: “The Girl from Ipanema,” sung by Astrud Gilberto, came off it.
fields.Gallery captions: With Chet Baker (right), 1983
fields.Clue: Saxophonist whose album with João Gilberto brought bossa nova to the United States.

fields.Title: Sonny Rollins
fields.Caption: In concert in Helsinki, 1972
fields.Notes: Saxophone Colossus, with “St. Thomas,” is his best-known album.
fields.Gallery captions: Rollins performing in Helsinki in 1972 | Rollins at the Newport Jazz Festival in 2008
fields.Clue: Saxophonist who took a two-year sabbatical practising on the Williamsburg Bridge.

fields.Title: Wynton Marsalis
fields.Caption: At the OSPAC Jazz Festival, West Orange, New Jersey, 2009
fields.Notes: His Blood on the Fields was the first jazz work to win the Pulitzer Prize; he runs Jazz at Lincoln Center.
fields.Captions: At the OSPAC Jazz Festival, West Orange, New Jersey, 2009
fields.Gallery captions: In concert in Lyon, 2016
fields.Clue: Trumpeter who won Grammys in jazz and in classical music in the same year.

fields.Title: Oscar Peterson
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1977
fields.Notes: His trio with Ray Brown was among the most recorded in jazz; he wrote the Canadiana Suite.
fields.Gallery captions: Peterson with Ella Fitzgerald, 1964 | Oscar Peterson Trio in 1959
fields.Clue: Prodigiously fast Canadian pianist, the house pianist for much of Verve's catalogue.

fields.Title: Django Reinhardt
fields.Caption: At the Aquarium jazz club, New York
fields.Notes: He founded the Quintette du Hot Club de France with the violinist Stéphane Grappelli.
fields.Captions: At the Aquarium jazz club, New York
fields.Gallery captions: Reinhardt and Duke Ellington at the Aquarium in New York, c. November 1946
fields.Clue: Romani guitarist who played with two fingers of his left hand after a caravan fire.

fields.Title: Chick Corea
fields.Caption: At the Kongsberg Jazz Festival, 2018
fields.Notes: “Spain” is his best-known tune.
fields.Clue: Pianist who played on Bitches Brew and led the fusion band Return to Forever.

fields.Title: Bud Powell
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1960
fields.Notes: He set the model for bebop piano; his later years were broken by mental illness and electroshock treatment.
fields.Clue: Pianist who translated Charlie Parker's bebop line to the keyboard.

fields.Title: Cab Calloway
fields.Caption: At the Columbia studio, New York
fields.Notes: He also wrote a Hepster's Dictionary of jive slang.
fields.Captions: At the Columbia studio, New York
fields.Gallery captions: Calloway by Carl Van Vechten, 1933 | Calloway (lower right) and his band in a railway sleeping car, 1933
fields.Clue: Cotton Club bandleader famous for the “hi-de-ho” call and response of “Minnie the Moocher.”

fields.Title: Count Basie
fields.Caption: Posed at the piano, 1955
fields.Notes: The section was Freddie Green, Walter Page, Jo Jones, and himself at the piano; “One O'Clock Jump” was his theme.
fields.Gallery captions: The Count Basie Orchestra in concert, 1962
fields.Clue: Kansas City bandleader whose rhythm section was so light it was called the All-American Rhythm Section.

fields.Title: Art Blakey
fields.Caption: At the drums
fields.Notes: Moanin' is the band's best-known record; its alumni include Lee Morgan, Wayne Shorter, and Wynton Marsalis.
fields.Gallery captions: Art Blakey, studio portrait | On the “Giants of Jazz” tour, Hamburg, 1973
fields.Clue: Drummer whose Jazz Messengers were a finishing school for hard bop.

fields.Title: Kind of Blue
fields.Caption: The original album cover
fields.Creator: Miles Davis
fields.Notes: Recorded in two sessions from sketches rather than charts, with John Coltrane, Cannonball Adderley, and Bill Evans.
fields.Gallery captions: Miles Davis, photographed by Tom Palumbo | Bill Evans, the album's pianist, 1961
fields.Clue: The best-selling jazz album ever made, built on modes instead of chord changes.

fields.Title: Bitches Brew
fields.Caption: The original album cover, painted by Mati Klarwein
fields.Creator: Miles Davis
fields.Notes: Teo Macero assembled it from long jams; the cover painting is by Mati Klarwein.
fields.Captions: The original album cover, painted by Mati Klarwein
fields.Clue: A double album whose electric instruments and studio editing turned jazz toward rock and split its audience.

fields.Title: A Love Supreme
fields.Caption: Coltrane's handwritten score
fields.Creator: John Coltrane
fields.Notes: Its parts are “Acknowledgement,” “Resolution,” “Pursuance,” and “Psalm”; McCoy Tyner and Elvin Jones play on it.
fields.Gallery captions: The album cover
fields.Clue: A four-part suite of thanksgiving in which the leader chants its title over a four-note bass figure.

fields.Title: Time Out
fields.Caption: The original album cover
fields.Creator: Dave Brubeck
fields.Notes: “Take Five” is in 5/4, and “Blue Rondo à la Turk” in 9/8.
fields.Clue: An album built on unusual metres, the first jazz album to sell a million copies.

fields.Title: Giant Steps
fields.Caption: The original album cover
fields.Creator: John Coltrane
fields.Notes: John Coltrane's first album entirely of his own compositions, including “Naima” and “Mr. P.C.”
fields.Gallery captions: Coltrane receiving an Edison Award for Giant Steps, Amsterdam, 1961
fields.Clue: Its title track cycles through keys a major third apart so fast that its changes are still a test piece.

fields.Title: Moanin'
fields.Caption: The album cover, as later reissued under the title Moanin'
fields.Creator: Art Blakey
fields.Notes: Lee Morgan and Benny Golson are on it.
fields.Captions: The original Blue Note album cover
fields.Clue: The definitive hard bop record, with Bobby Timmons's gospel-inflected title tune.

fields.Title: The Shape of Jazz to Come
fields.Caption: The original album cover
fields.Creator: Ornette Coleman
fields.Notes: Don Cherry plays pocket trumpet; its title was a manifesto.
fields.Clue: A quartet album with no piano, so that no instrument fixed the harmony, opening with “Lonely Woman.”

fields.Title: Head Hunters
fields.Caption: The original album cover
fields.Creator: Herbie Hancock
fields.Notes: The first jazz album to go platinum; it remakes “Watermelon Man.”
fields.Clue: A jazz-funk album with synthesizers, opening with the fifteen-minute “Chameleon.”

fields.Title: Mingus Ah Um
fields.Caption: The original album cover
fields.Creator: Charles Mingus
fields.Notes: It also holds “Better Git It in Your Soul” and “Goodbye Pork Pie Hat,” an elegy for Lester Young.
fields.Clue: Its “Fables of Faubus” mocked the segregationist governor of Arkansas.

fields.Title: “Strange Fruit”
fields.Caption: The original Commodore 78 rpm label
fields.Creator: Billie Holiday
fields.Notes: Billie Holiday recorded it for Commodore in 1939, and closed her shows with it.
fields.Gallery captions: Billie Holiday's original Commodore 78, 1939
fields.Clue: A song about lynching, written by the schoolteacher Abel Meeropol, that Columbia refused to record.

fields.Title: “Body and Soul”
fields.Caption: Coleman Hawkins, who recorded it in 1939, photographed by William P. Gottlieb about 1946
fields.Creator: Coleman Hawkins
fields.Notes: Coleman Hawkins's tenor saxophone recording.
fields.Clue: A 1939 recording that barely states the melody, treated as the founding document of the jazz ballad solo.

fields.Title: “Take Five”
fields.Caption: Dave Brubeck, whose quartet recorded it, in 1964
fields.Creator: Paul Desmond
fields.Notes: Paul Desmond wrote it for the Dave Brubeck Quartet's Time Out.
fields.Gallery captions: The Dave Brubeck Quartet, with Paul Desmond, its composer, 1967
fields.Clue: A piece in 5/4 that became the best-selling jazz single ever released.

fields.Title: “Maple Leaf Rag”
fields.Caption: The first edition's sheet-music cover, 1899
fields.Creator: Scott Joplin
fields.Notes: Scott Joplin named it for the Maple Leaf Club in Sedalia, Missouri.
fields.Gallery captions: The cover of the first edition, 1899
fields.Clue: A rag of 1899 that sold in the hundreds of thousands as sheet music, and made its composer's name.

fields.Title: Sarah Vaughan
fields.Caption: Possibly at Café Society, New York
fields.Notes: Nicknamed Sassy and the Divine One; she started with Earl Hines's band as singer and second pianist.
fields.Captions: Possibly at Café Society, New York
fields.Gallery captions: Vaughan in 1955 | Vaughan in 1978
fields.Clue: Singer with the widest range and most operatic technique of the great jazz singers.

fields.Title: Fats Waller
fields.Caption: At the piano
fields.Notes: He also played the organ, and was once kidnapped to play at Al Capone's birthday party.
fields.Clue: Stride pianist and comic performer who wrote “Ain't Misbehavin'” and “Honeysuckle Rose.”

fields.Title: Jelly Roll Morton
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph, Chicago, c. 1927
fields.Notes: His Red Hot Peppers sides are the first great jazz arrangements.
fields.Gallery captions: An Edison disc of “The Jelly Roll Blues”, recorded by the Original Memphis Five
fields.Clue: Pianist who claimed to have invented jazz in 1902.

fields.Title: Sidney Bechet
fields.Caption: With Freddie Moore and Lloyd Phillips at Jimmy Ryan's, New York
fields.Notes: He also played clarinet; “Petite Fleur” was his late hit in France.
fields.Captions: With Freddie Moore and Lloyd Phillips at Jimmy Ryan's, New York
fields.Gallery captions: Bechet in 1922
fields.Clue: New Orleans soprano saxophonist, the first important jazz soloist on record, who made his name in Paris.

fields.Title: Bix Beiderbecke
fields.Caption: At Doyle's Academy of Music, Cincinnati
fields.Notes: “Singin' the Blues” and the piano piece “In a Mist” are his best-known recordings.
fields.Captions: At Doyle's Academy of Music, Cincinnati
fields.Clue: Cornetist, the first widely admired white jazz soloist, dead at twenty-eight.

fields.Title: Coleman Hawkins
fields.Caption: From a Billboard advertisement, 1945
fields.Notes: His 1939 “Body and Soul” is the founding jazz ballad solo; he was nicknamed Hawk and Bean.
fields.Gallery captions: Coleman Hawkins, c. September 1946
fields.Clue: Saxophonist who made the tenor a jazz instrument.

fields.Title: Lester Young
fields.Caption: At the Spotlite club, New York, about 1946, photographed by William P. Gottlieb
fields.Notes: He named Billie Holiday “Lady Day,” and she named him “Pres.”
fields.Gallery captions: At the Famous Door, New York, c. 1946
fields.Clue: Tenor saxophonist whose light, behind-the-beat tone opposed Coleman Hawkins's and pointed toward cool jazz.

fields.Title: Max Roach
fields.Caption: At the Three Deuces, New York, c. 1947
fields.Notes: He made We Insist! Max Roach's Freedom Now Suite with Abbey Lincoln, and co-led a quintet with Clifford Brown.
fields.Captions: At the Three Deuces, New York, c. 1947
fields.Gallery captions: Roach in 2000
fields.Clue: Drummer who moved bebop timekeeping to the ride cymbal.

fields.Title: Elvin Jones
fields.Caption: Portrait photograph
fields.Notes: He plays on A Love Supreme.
fields.Clue: Drummer who was the polyrhythmic engine of the John Coltrane Quartet.

fields.Title: Clifford Brown
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1956
fields.Notes: He co-led a quintet with Max Roach, and was one of the few major jazz musicians of his day with no drug habit.
fields.Gallery captions: Max Roach, his co-leader in the Clifford Brown–Max Roach Quintet
fields.Clue: Hard bop's cleanest trumpet voice, killed in a car crash at twenty-five.

fields.Title: Eric Dolphy
fields.Notes: Out to Lunch! is his masterpiece; he died at thirty-six.
fields.Gallery captions: In his graduation cap, 1947
fields.Clue: Multi-instrumentalist who played alto saxophone, bass clarinet, and flute at the edge of tonality.

fields.Title: Wes Montgomery
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph for Verve Records, mid-1960s
fields.Notes: The Incredible Jazz Guitar of Wes Montgomery is his best-known record.
fields.Captions: Publicity photograph for Verve Records, mid-1960s
fields.Gallery captions: In a Gibson guitar advertisement, 1967 | Montgomery in 1965
fields.Clue: Guitarist who played with his thumb rather than a pick, and made octaves a signature.

fields.Title: Freddie Hubbard
fields.Caption: In Rochester, New York, 1976
fields.Notes: He also plays on Herbie Hancock's Maiden Voyage.
fields.Gallery captions: Hubbard at the Great American Music Hall, San Francisco, 1977
fields.Clue: Hard bop trumpeter who played on both Coltrane's Ascension and Ornette Coleman's Free Jazz.

fields.Title: Wayne Shorter
fields.Caption: With Weather Report, Amsterdam, 1980
fields.Notes: Speak No Evil is his own best record.
fields.Gallery captions: The Wayne Shorter Quartet in Milan, 2010
fields.Clue: Saxophonist who wrote for the Jazz Messengers and Miles Davis's second quintet, then co-founded Weather Report.

fields.Title: Ron Carter
fields.Caption: At the UC Berkeley Jazz Festival, 1980
fields.Notes: He has appeared on more than two thousand recordings.
fields.Captions: At the UC Berkeley Jazz Festival, 1980
fields.Gallery captions: At the European Jazz Expo, 2007 | At the Newport Jazz Festival, 2009
fields.Clue: The most recorded bassist in jazz, and the anchor of Miles Davis's second quintet.

fields.Title: McCoy Tyner
fields.Caption: At the piano in concert
fields.Notes: He left the quartet in 1965, as Coltrane moved into free playing.
fields.Clue: Pianist whose quartal voicings and heavy left hand were the harmonic foundation of the John Coltrane Quartet.

fields.Title: Keith Jarrett
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph, Los Angeles, 1975
fields.Notes: That album is The Köln Concert, released by ECM in 1975.
fields.Gallery captions: With Miles Davis's band, 1971
fields.Clue: Pianist whose improvised concert on a badly out-of-tune piano is the best-selling solo album in jazz.

fields.Title: Pat Metheny
fields.Caption: With the Orchestrion Project, Grand Prairie, Texas, 2010
fields.Notes: He records for ECM with the Pat Metheny Group, and built a mechanical Orchestrion to play with.
fields.Captions: With the Orchestrion Project, Grand Prairie, Texas, 2010
fields.Gallery captions: Metheny at KJAZ radio, Alameda, California, December 1980 | With Steve Rodby (left)
fields.Clue: Guitarist who has won Grammys in more categories than any other artist.

fields.Title: Cecil Taylor
fields.Caption: At the Moers Festival, 2008
fields.Notes: Unit Structures is the reference point for free-jazz piano.
fields.Gallery captions: Cecil Taylor, Buffalo, New York
fields.Clue: Pianist who treated the piano as eighty-eight tuned drums.
