fields.Notes: Christopher Wheeldon's ballet after Lewis Carroll, now a repertory staple.
fields.Clue: The Royal Ballet's first new full-length narrative ballet in decades, with a score by Joby Talbot and a tap-dancing Mad Hatter.

fields.Title: Flight Pattern
fields.Caption: A performance of the work
fields.Creator: Crystal Pite
fields.Notes: Crystal Pite's first work for the Royal Ballet.
fields.Gallery captions: Crystal Pite, its choreographer, 2010
fields.Clue: Thirty-six dancers respond to the refugee crisis, to the first movement of Górecki's Third Symphony.

fields.Title: Tango
fields.Caption: A tango show in Buenos Aires
fields.Notes: The root of both the ballroom and the Argentine styles; Astor Piazzolla's nuevo tango reworked its music.
fields.Captions: Dancers at a tango festival in Montevideo, Uruguay
fields.Gallery captions: Tango postcard, c. 1919
fields.Clue: A partner dance born in the port districts of Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

fields.Title: Pas de deux
fields.Caption: Dancers in the Paquita grand pas de deux
fields.Notes: The grand pas de deux of The Nutcracker and Don Quixote are gala staples.
fields.Captions: Dancers in the Paquita grand pas de deux
fields.Gallery captions: The grand pas de deux from The Nutcracker, 2011
fields.Clue: A duet that is the structural centrepiece of classical ballet: an adagio, two solo variations, and a coda.

fields.Title: Arabesque
fields.Caption: A dancer in arabesque on pointe
fields.Notes: The defining line of classical ballet; in the penchée form the body tips forward.
fields.Clue: A position in which the dancer stands on one leg with the other extended straight behind.

fields.Title: Pointe technique
fields.Caption: A foot en pointe in a pointe shoe
fields.Notes: Marie Taglioni's La Sylphide made it the emblem of the Romantic ballerina.
fields.Captions: A foot en pointe in a pointe shoe
fields.Gallery captions: A dancer en pointe, her weight carried over the tips of the toes
fields.Clue: Dancing on the tips of fully extended feet, in blocked shoes.

fields.Title: Lev Ivanov
fields.Caption: Photographed in Saint Petersburg
fields.Notes: With Petipa ill, he also staged The Nutcracker.
fields.Clue: Marius Petipa's second ballet master, who choreographed the lakeside acts of the 1895 Swan Lake.

fields.Title: August Bournonville
fields.Caption: Painted portrait, 1828
fields.Notes: His La Sylphide and Napoli are still danced as he made them.
fields.Clue: Choreographer who led the Royal Danish Ballet for nearly fifty years, in a style of light, quick footwork and buoyant jumps.

fields.Title: Jules Perrot
fields.Caption: London, c. 1850
fields.Notes: He later became ballet master in Saint Petersburg; Degas painted him rehearsing.
fields.Gallery captions: “The Opera Polka as danced by Mlle. Carlotta Grisi & Mons. Perrot” (Boston: William H. Oakes, ca. 1840s) | Edgar Degas, The Dance Class, 1874: Perrot, with his cane, rehearsing dancers at the Paris Opéra
fields.Clue: Choreographer who made Giselle's own dances, and a Pas de Quatre for four rival star ballerinas.

fields.Title: Jean Coralli
fields.Caption: Engraved portrait, c. 1810
fields.Notes: He also made Le Diable boiteux for Fanny Elssler.
fields.Gallery captions: Jean Coralli, circa 1830
fields.Clue: Paris Opera ballet master who created Giselle with Jules Perrot.

fields.Title: Bronislava Nijinska
fields.Caption: Graduation photograph, 1908
fields.Notes: Vaslav Nijinsky's sister, and one of the first women to choreograph for a major company.
fields.Clue: Choreographer of Les Noces and Les Biches for the Ballets Russes, and sister of its star.

fields.Title: Christopher Wheeldon
fields.Caption: At the 75th Tony Awards, 2022
fields.Notes: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland and The Winter's Tale are his; he won a Tony for An American in Paris.
fields.Clue: Choreographer of full-length story ballets for the Royal Ballet.

fields.Title: Justin Peck
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2018
fields.Notes: He won Tonys for the 2018 Carousel, Illinoise, and Buena Vista Social Club.
fields.Clue: Resident choreographer of New York City Ballet since 2014, only the second person to hold the post.

fields.Title: Ohad Naharin
fields.Caption: At the Herzliya Conference
fields.Notes: He directed the Batsheva Dance Company from 1990 to 2018.
fields.Gallery captions: Batsheva Dance Company | Ohad Naharin instructing dancers
fields.Clue: Israeli choreographer who created the Gaga movement language.

fields.Title: Jiří Kylián
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2020
fields.Notes: Sinfonietta and Petite Mort are his best-known works.
fields.Clue: Czech choreographer who directed Nederlands Dans Theater from 1975 to 1999.

fields.Title: Maurice Béjart
fields.Caption: Photographed by Erling Mandelmann, 1988
fields.Notes: He directed the Ballet of the 20th Century in Brussels, and then his own company in Lausanne.
fields.Gallery captions: Directing dancers in Pli selon pli, Brussels, 1976
fields.Clue: Choreographer whose Boléro is danced on a round table.

fields.Title: Roland Petit
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2009
fields.Notes: He made Carmen in 1949 for his Ballets de Paris.
fields.Clue: French choreographer of Le Jeune Homme et la Mort, to a scenario by Jean Cocteau.

fields.Title: Anna Sokolow
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1961
fields.Notes: She helped establish modern dance in Mexico and Israel.
fields.Clue: Martha Graham dancer whose Rooms set urban loneliness to a jazz score.

fields.Title: Gower Champion
fields.Caption: Press photograph, 1962
fields.Notes: Bye Bye Birdie, Hello, Dolly!, and 42nd Street.
fields.Clue: Director-choreographer of a run of Broadway hits, who died on the day his last one opened.

fields.Title: Susan Stroman
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2007
fields.Notes: Choreography for Crazy for You, Show Boat, Contact, and The Producers, which she also directed.
fields.Clue: Winner of five Tonys, four for choreography and one for directing, two of them for the same show.

fields.Title: Rudolf Laban
fields.Caption: Laban (seated) with his dancers, 1914
fields.Notes: A founder of German expressionist dance; Mary Wigman and Kurt Jooss studied with him.
fields.Clue: Theorist who devised the standard system of dance notation, which bears his name.

fields.Title: Mary Wigman
fields.Caption: Photographed by Jacob Merkelbach, 1922
fields.Notes: A pupil of Rudolf Laban.
fields.Gallery captions: In 1946 | At Monte Verità, on Lake Maggiore, while studying with Rudolf Laban
fields.Clue: Pioneer of German expressionist dance, Ausdruckstanz, whose masked Witch Dance is her signature solo.

fields.Title: Natalia Makarova
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1971
fields.Notes: She joined American Ballet Theatre, and staged its first full-length La Bayadère in 1980.
fields.Gallery captions: At the Kennedy Center Honors, 2012
fields.Clue: Kirov ballerina who defected in London in 1970.

fields.Title: Galina Ulanova
fields.Caption: With Yuri Zhdanov in Romeo and Juliet
fields.Notes: She led the Bolshoi's first London season, in 1956.
fields.Captions: With Yuri Zhdanov in Romeo and Juliet
fields.Gallery captions: At a press conference in Amsterdam, 1968
fields.Clue: The leading Soviet ballerina of her era, who created Juliet in Leonid Lavrovsky's Romeo and Juliet.

fields.Title: Maya Plisetskaya
fields.Caption: In Swan Lake with the Bolshoi Ballet, 1966
fields.Notes: Famed as Odette-Odile; her husband was the composer Rodion Shchedrin.
fields.Captions: In Swan Lake with the Bolshoi Ballet, 1966
fields.Gallery captions: At the Bolshoi Theatre, 2005 | Plisetskaya in 1953 | Plisetskaya in Carmen Suite, 1974
fields.Clue: Bolshoi ballerina for whom Alberto Alonso made Carmen Suite, to her husband's arrangement of Bizet.

fields.Title: Suzanne Farrell
fields.Caption: With New York City Ballet in Amsterdam, c. 1965
fields.Notes: He also made his Don Quixote on her, dancing the Don himself at the premiere.
fields.Captions: With New York City Ballet in Amsterdam, c. 1965
fields.Gallery captions: Farrell in 1965 | With George Balanchine in Don Quixote
fields.Clue: George Balanchine's muse of the 1960s, on whom he made the Diamonds section of Jewels.

fields.Title: Alicia Alonso
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1955
fields.Notes: Her company, founded in 1948, became the Ballet Nacional de Cuba in 1959.
fields.Gallery captions: With the conductor Benjamin Steinberg and the Ballet Nacional de Cuba | By Annemarie Heinrich, 1958
fields.Clue: Cuban prima ballerina assoluta who went on dancing Giselle though nearly blind.

fields.Title: Sylvie Guillem
fields.Caption: With Russell Maliphant
fields.Notes: William Forsythe made In the Middle, Somewhat Elevated on her; she later guested with the Royal Ballet.
fields.Clue: Made an étoile of the Paris Opera Ballet by Rudolf Nureyev at nineteen.

fields.Title: Carlos Acosta
fields.Caption: At the Goya Awards, 2019
fields.Notes: He went on to direct Birmingham Royal Ballet.
fields.Clue: Cuban dancer who was a principal of the Royal Ballet from 1998 to 2015.

fields.Title: Tamara Karsavina
fields.Caption: As Armide in Le Pavillon d'Armide
fields.Notes: She settled in London and helped found British ballet.
fields.Gallery captions: In Saint Petersburg, c. 1915 | Karsavina, c. 1910
fields.Clue: Ballets Russes ballerina who created the Firebird and the Ballerina in Petrushka.

fields.Title: Alicia Markova
fields.Caption: Photographed by Carl Van Vechten, 1940
fields.Notes: With Anton Dolin she co-founded Festival Ballet, now English National Ballet, in 1950.
fields.Gallery captions: In the Bluebird pas de deux from The Sleeping Beauty, Ballet Theatre, 1941 | In The Dying Swan, 1948
fields.Clue: The first British dancer to take the roles of Giselle and Odette-Odile, with the Vic-Wells Ballet in 1934.

fields.Title: Judith Jamison
fields.Caption: At Elon University, 2012
fields.Notes: She directed his company from 1989 to 2011.
fields.Clue: Alvin Ailey's muse, for whom he made the solo Cry.

fields.Title: Ginger Rogers
fields.Caption: Photographed by John Miehle
fields.Notes: From Flying Down to Rio to The Barkleys of Broadway; her Oscar was for Kitty Foyle.
fields.Gallery captions: With Fred Astaire in Follow the Fleet, 1936
fields.Clue: Fred Astaire's partner in ten films, who won the Best Actress Oscar for a role with no dancing in it.

fields.Title: Savion Glover
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2007
fields.Notes: He danced the steps of Mumble the penguin in Happy Feet.
fields.Clue: Tap dancer who won a Tony for choreographing Bring in 'da Noise, Bring in 'da Funk.

fields.Title: Gregory Hines
fields.Caption: In Baltimore, 1993
fields.Notes: He won a Tony for playing Jelly Roll Morton in Jelly's Last Jam.
fields.Clue: Tap dancer who starred in the film Tap alongside the old masters of the form.

fields.Title: Ann Miller
fields.Caption: CBS publicity photograph for The Big Record, 1957
fields.Notes: Easter Parade, On the Town, and Kiss Me Kate.
fields.Captions: CBS publicity photograph for The Big Record, 1957
fields.Gallery captions: RKO publicity portrait | In 1938
fields.Clue: MGM's fastest tap dancer, publicized as tapping five hundred times a minute.

fields.Title: Josephine Baker
fields.Caption: In her banana skirt at the Folies Bergère, 1927
fields.Notes: She worked for the French Resistance, and in 2021 became the first Black woman in the Panthéon.
fields.Clue: Dancer who performed at the Folies Bergère in a skirt of bananas.

fields.Title: Lorenz Hart
fields.Caption: New York World-Telegram photograph, 1936
fields.Notes: “Blue Moon,” “The Lady Is a Tramp,” “Manhattan,” “Bewitched, Bothered and Bewildered,” and “My Funny Valentine.”
fields.Clue: Richard Rodgers's lyricist before Oscar Hammerstein II.

fields.Title: George Gershwin
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1937
fields.Notes: Rhapsody in Blue for Paul Whiteman, An American in Paris, Porgy and Bess, and songs with his brother Ira such as “I Got Rhythm.”
fields.Gallery captions: At a birthday party for Maurice Ravel, New York, 1928
fields.Clue: Composer who bridged the concert hall and Tin Pan Alley, and died at thirty-eight.

fields.Title: Ira Gershwin
fields.Caption: Ira Gershwin (right) with his brother George
fields.Notes: “I Got Rhythm,” “Embraceable You,” and “Someone to Watch Over Me”; he wrote the lyrics of Porgy and Bess with DuBose Heyward.
fields.Gallery captions: George and Ira Gershwin in 1930
fields.Clue: Lyricist who wrote more than a dozen Broadway shows with his younger brother.

fields.Title: Bertolt Brecht
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1954
fields.Notes: He wrote The Threepenny Opera with Kurt Weill, and founded the Berliner Ensemble.
fields.Clue: Playwright who developed epic theatre and the alienation effect.

fields.Title: Leonard Bernstein
fields.Caption: Photographed by Jack Mitchell, 1977
fields.Notes: West Side Story, Candide, and On the Town.
fields.Gallery captions: With Benny Goodman in rehearsal
fields.Clue: Composer who led the New York Philharmonic and hosted its televised Young People's Concerts while writing for Broadway.

fields.Title: John Kander
fields.Caption: At Sardi's
fields.Notes: Cabaret, Chicago, and Kiss of the Spider Woman.
fields.Clue: The composer to Fred Ebb's lyrics, a partnership that produced “New York, New York.”

fields.Title: Frederick Loewe
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1962
fields.Notes: Brigadoon, Paint Your Wagon, My Fair Lady, and Camelot, and the film Gigi.
fields.Clue: The Austrian-born composer who set Alan Jay Lerner's words, and retired early after their partnership ended.

fields.Title: Tim Rice
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2020
fields.Notes: Jesus Christ Superstar and Evita, Chess, and The Lion King and Aida.
fields.Clue: Lyricist who wrote for Andrew Lloyd Webber, then for Elton John, and for ABBA's two songwriters.

fields.Title: Stephen Schwartz
fields.Caption: At the opening night of Funny Girl, 2022
fields.Notes: Godspell, Pippin, and Wicked, and lyrics for Disney's Pocahontas and The Hunchback of Notre Dame.
fields.Captions: At the opening night of Funny Girl, 2022
fields.Clue: Composer whose score for the highest-grossing Broadway show of the 2000s retold Oz.

fields.Title: Marvin Hamlisch
fields.Caption: Agency publicity photograph, 1970s
fields.Notes: The Pulitzer was for A Chorus Line; he scored The Way We Were and adapted Scott Joplin for The Sting.
fields.Gallery captions: At 29, with two of his three 1974 Oscars, alongside Donald O'Connor, Debbie Reynolds, and Cher | Hamlisch conducting
fields.Clue: Composer who held the Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony, plus a Pulitzer.

fields.Title: Cy Coleman
fields.Caption: Washington, D.C., 1996
fields.Notes: Sweet Charity, Barnum, and City of Angels.
fields.Gallery captions: With Neil Simon (right) in rehearsal, 1982
fields.Clue: Composer and jazz pianist who wrote “Big Spender.”

fields.Title: Meredith Willson
fields.Caption: Promotional photograph for The Unsinkable Molly Brown, 1961
fields.Notes: The Music Man and The Unsinkable Molly Brown; he also wrote “It's Beginning to Look a Lot Like Christmas.”
fields.Captions: Promotional photograph for The Unsinkable Molly Brown, 1961
fields.Gallery captions: Willson in 1937 | Robert Preston as Harold Hill in The Music Man
fields.Clue: Composer who wrote the book, music, and lyrics of a musical about a con man in Iowa.

fields.Title: Sheldon Harnick
fields.Caption: Photographed in 2006
fields.Notes: Fiorello!, She Loves Me, and Fiddler on the Roof.
fields.Clue: The lyricist to Jerry Bock's music, a partnership that ended after a dispute over a 1970 show.

fields.Title: Betty Comden
fields.Caption: Photographed c. 1960
fields.Notes: With Adolph Green: On the Town, Bells Are Ringing, and the screenplay of Singin' in the Rain.
fields.Clue: The female half of Broadway's longest writing partnership, which began in the nightclub act The Revuers and ran for six decades.

fields.Title: Adolph Green
fields.Caption: At the Kennedy Center Honors, Washington, D.C.
fields.Notes: With Betty Comden: On the Town, Wonderful Town, and the screenplay of Singin' in the Rain.
fields.Captions: At the Kennedy Center Honors, Washington, D.C.
fields.Gallery captions: Leonard Bernstein, their collaborator on On the Town and Wonderful Town | Gene Kelly in Singin' in the Rain, 1952, which Comden and Green wrote
fields.Clue: The male half of Broadway's longest writing partnership, which began in the nightclub act The Revuers and ran for six decades.

fields.Title: Arthur Laurents
fields.Caption: Before the marquee of La Cage aux Folles, which he directed
fields.Notes: West Side Story and Gypsy; he also wrote the screenplay of The Way We Were.
fields.Captions: Before the marquee of La Cage aux Folles, which he directed
fields.Gallery captions: Laurents in 2009
fields.Clue: Librettist who wrote the books of two Jerome Robbins musicals, one about gangs and one about a stage mother.

fields.Title: Julie Taymor
fields.Caption: At the Tokyo International Film Festival, 2022
fields.Notes: That musical was The Lion King; she also directed the films Frida and Across the Universe.
fields.Captions: At the Tokyo International Film Festival, 2022
fields.Gallery captions: At the Metropolitan Opera, 2009
fields.Clue: The first woman to win the Tony for directing a musical, working in masks and puppets.

fields.Title: Ethel Merman
fields.Caption: Photographed for the New York World-Telegram and Sun
fields.Notes: Anything Goes, Annie Get Your Gun, and Call Me Madam; she created Mama Rose in Gypsy.
fields.Gallery captions: Poster for Alexander's Ragtime Band, 1938, in which she co-starred
fields.Clue: Brassy belter whom Cole Porter and Irving Berlin wrote for, and who never needed a microphone.

fields.Title: Angela Lansbury
fields.Caption: Studio publicity photograph, 1950
fields.Notes: Tonys for Mame, Dear World, Gypsy, and Sweeney Todd, and a fifth for the play Blithe Spirit.
fields.Gallery captions: In Till the Clouds Roll By, 1946, one of her first films
fields.Clue: Actress who created Mrs. Lovett, and spent twelve years playing a mystery writer on television.

fields.Title: Patti LuPone
fields.Caption: From a video interview
fields.Notes: Tonys for Evita, Gypsy, and Company; she created Fantine in the original London Les Misérables.
fields.Clue: Performer who created Eva Perón in London, and is known for stopping performances over audience phones.

fields.Title: Bernadette Peters
fields.Caption: At the Broadway opening night of Old Friends, 2025
fields.Notes: Sunday in the Park with George and Into the Woods; Tonys for Song and Dance and Annie Get Your Gun.
fields.Captions: At the Broadway opening night of Old Friends, 2025
fields.Gallery captions: On The Tim Conway Show, 1980 | In Pennies from Heaven, 1981
fields.Clue: Stephen Sondheim's leading lady, who created both Dot and the Witch.

fields.Title: Audra McDonald
fields.Caption: At the 74th Tony Awards, 2021
fields.Notes: She played Billie Holiday in Lady Day at Emerson's Bar and Grill in 2014.
fields.Gallery captions: McDonald in 1998
fields.Clue: Performer with six Tony Awards, the only person to win in all four acting categories.

fields.Title: Chita Rivera
fields.Caption: At Lena Horne's 80th birthday party, New York, 1997
fields.Notes: Tonys for The Rink and Kiss of the Spider Woman.
fields.Captions: At Lena Horne's 80th birthday party, New York, 1997
fields.Gallery captions: Paula Kelly (third from right) and Chita Rivera (second from right) in Sweet Charity, 1969
fields.Clue: Performer who created Anita and Velma Kelly, and was the first Latina to receive a Kennedy Center Honor.

fields.Title: Fletcher Henderson
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph, 1943
fields.Notes: Don Redman arranged for the orchestra, and Louis Armstrong and Coleman Hawkins played in it.
fields.Gallery captions: His orchestra in 1925, with Coleman Hawkins (seated, far left) and Louis Armstrong (above him)
fields.Clue: Bandleader whose New York orchestra set the big-band swing format, and whose later charts built Benny Goodman's book.

fields.Title: Art Tatum
fields.Caption: At the Vogue Room, New York, c. 1946–48
fields.Notes: He left Toledo in 1932, and held solo residencies in New York, Chicago, and Los Angeles.
fields.Captions: At the Vogue Room, New York, c. 1946–48
fields.Clue: Nearly blind pianist widely regarded as the greatest virtuoso of jazz piano.

fields.Title: Albert Ayler
fields.Caption: At a session at Capitol Studios, New York, c. 1967–68
fields.Notes: Spiritual Unity is his best-known record; he was found dead in New York's East River in 1970.
fields.Captions: At a session at Capitol Studios, New York, c. 1967–68
fields.Clue: Free-jazz tenor saxophonist who set hymn-like themes against a huge, wide vibrato.

fields.Title: Pharoah Sanders
fields.Caption: Photographed in December 2006
fields.Notes: The leading voice of spiritual jazz after Coltrane.
fields.Gallery captions: Pharoah Sanders in 1981 | Sanders performing at The Jazz Cafe in London, England, 2008
fields.Clue: Saxophonist from John Coltrane's last bands whose Karma holds “The Creator Has a Master Plan.”

fields.Title: Mary Lou Williams
fields.Caption: Photographed by William P. Gottlieb, c. 1946
fields.Notes: She arranged for Andy Kirk's Clouds of Joy.
fields.Captions: Photographed by William P. Gottlieb, c. 1946
fields.Gallery captions: Williams in her apartment with Jack Teagarden, Tadd Dameron, Hank Jones, and Dizzy Gillespie | By Lynn Gilbert, 1978
fields.Clue: Pianist and arranger who wrote the Zodiac Suite and mentored Thelonious Monk, Bud Powell, and Dizzy Gillespie.

fields.Title: Betty Carter
fields.Caption: At the Pori Jazz Festival, Finland, 1978
fields.Notes: John Hicks and Mulgrew Miller came through her groups.
fields.Captions: At the Pori Jazz Festival, Finland, 1978
fields.Gallery captions: Carter at the Great American Music Hall, San Francisco, California, 1979 | Carter in 1981
fields.Clue: Bebop singer known for radical reworkings of standards, whose trios trained young pianists.

fields.Title: Anita O'Day
fields.Caption: Headshot, 1955
fields.Notes: She sang with Gene Krupa's and Stan Kenton's bands.
fields.Clue: Singer whose “Sweet Georgia Brown” at the 1958 Newport festival is preserved in Jazz on a Summer's Day.

fields.Title: Gerry Mulligan
fields.Caption: Photographed in the 1980s
fields.Notes: He also arranged for Miles Davis's Birth of the Cool.
fields.Gallery captions: Mulligan on piano in the Netherlands in 1960 | Gerry Mulligan at the Monterey Jazz Festival, 1992
fields.Clue: Baritone saxophonist whose pianoless quartet with Chet Baker defined West Coast cool.

fields.Title: Chet Baker
fields.Caption: Publicity photograph, 1955
fields.Notes: He was first known in Gerry Mulligan's pianoless quartet.
fields.Gallery captions: With Stan Getz, 1983 | Baker in 1983
fields.Clue: Trumpeter and singer called the Prince of Cool, whose signature was “My Funny Valentine.”

fields.Title: Horace Silver
fields.Caption: In Los Angeles
fields.Notes: “Song for My Father” is his best-known tune.
fields.Gallery captions: Silver c. 1965 | Silver at Keystone Korner, San Francisco, in 1978
fields.Clue: Hard bop pianist who co-founded the Jazz Messengers with Art Blakey.

fields.Title: Cannonball Adderley
fields.Caption: Press photograph, 1966
fields.Notes: He played on Kind of Blue; his brother Nat played cornet in his band.
fields.Gallery captions: With his brother Nat (left), Amsterdam, 1961
fields.Clue: Alto saxophonist whose quintet had a 1966 hit with Joe Zawinul's “Mercy, Mercy, Mercy.”

fields.Title: Jaco Pastorius
fields.Caption: In Amsterdam, 1980
fields.Notes: “Birdland” and Heavy Weather, and Joni Mitchell's Hejira.
fields.Gallery captions: Jaco Pastorius in concert, c. 1980
fields.Clue: Fretless electric bassist of Weather Report.

fields.Title: Benny Carter
fields.Caption: Photographed in 1984
fields.Notes: He wrote film scores in Hollywood, and played into his nineties.
fields.Gallery captions: With Robert Goffin, Louis Armstrong, and Leonard Feather, 1942 | At the Apollo Theater, New York, c. 1946
fields.Clue: With Johnny Hodges, a pioneer of the alto saxophone, who also played trumpet and arranged.

fields.Title: Roy Eldridge
fields.Caption: At the Spotlite Club, New York
fields.Notes: Nicknamed Little Jazz, he played with Gene Krupa and Artie Shaw.
fields.Captions: At the Spotlite Club, New York
fields.Clue: Swing trumpeter whose fast, high, harmonically daring solos led from Louis Armstrong to Dizzy Gillespie.

fields.Title: Raymonda
fields.Caption: Title page of Glazunov's piano score
fields.Creator: Marius Petipa
fields.Notes: Set to Alexander Glazunov's score; Pierina Legnani created the title role.
fields.Captions: Title page of Glazunov's piano score
fields.Gallery captions: Pierina Legnani, the original Raymonda, 1898 | Title page for the 1898 premiere, with music by Alexander Glazunov
fields.Clue: A ballet whose Act III Pas classique hongrois is often performed on its own.

fields.Title: Cinderella
fields.Caption: Aleksandra Liashenko in Ashton's production, Polish National Ballet, 2010
fields.Creator: Frederick Ashton
fields.Notes: Set to Prokofiev's score, first danced at the Bolshoi in 1945; this version was made for Sadler's Wells in 1948.
fields.Captions: Aleksandra Liashenko in Ashton's production, Polish National Ballet, 2010
fields.Clue: The first full-length ballet by a British choreographer, who played one of the Ugly Sisters himself, with Robert Helpmann as the other.

fields.Title: Les Noces
fields.Caption: Cover of a full-score edition
fields.Creator: Bronislava Nijinska
fields.Notes: Set to Stravinsky's score, for the Ballets Russes.
fields.Clue: A Russian peasant wedding set as a ballet-cantata for voices, percussion, and four pianos.

fields.Title: Concerto Barocco
fields.Caption: A performance of Balanchine's choreography
fields.Creator: George Balanchine
fields.Notes: Made for American Ballet Caravan's South American tour of 1941.
fields.Clue: A plotless setting of Bach's D minor work for two violins, for eleven dancers.

fields.Title: Camelot
fields.Caption: Julie Andrews as Guenevere in the original production, 1960
fields.Creator: Alan Jay Lerner and Frederick Loewe
fields.Notes: Lerner and Loewe's show, after T. H. White's The Once and Future King.
fields.Captions: Julie Andrews as Guenevere in the original production, 1960
fields.Gallery captions: The original Broadway cast, including, foreground, from left, Robert Goulet, Julie Andrews, and Richard Burton.
fields.Clue: King Arthur's court and his queen's love for Lancelot, first played by Richard Burton and Julie Andrews.

fields.Title: Mame
fields.Caption: Angela Lansbury, the original Mame
fields.Creator: Jerry Herman
fields.Venue: Winter Garden Theatre, New York City
fields.Notes: Jerry Herman's musical, from Patrick Dennis's novel.
fields.Clue: An orphaned boy is raised through the Depression by his eccentric aunt, a role that won Angela Lansbury a Tony.

fields.Title: Pippin
fields.Caption: A scene from a 2017 production
fields.Creator: Stephen Schwartz
fields.Notes: Stephen Schwartz's score; Bob Fosse directed and choreographed the original.
fields.Clue: A Leading Player and a troupe tell the story of Charlemagne's son searching for fulfilment.

fields.Title: Hair
fields.Caption: The 2016–2017 Montreal production
fields.Creator: Galt MacDermot, Gerome Ragni, and James Rado
fields.Notes: “Aquarius” and “Let the Sunshine In” came from it.
fields.Clue: “The American Tribal Love-Rock Musical,” with a nude scene and songs against the Vietnam War.

fields.Title: Miss Saigon
fields.Caption: At Her Majesty's Theatre, Melbourne
fields.Creator: Claude-Michel Schönberg and Alain Boublil
fields.Notes: Claude-Michel Schönberg and Alain Boublil's follow-up to Les Misérables.
fields.Clue: Madama Butterfly moved to the end of the Vietnam War, with a helicopter landing on stage.

fields.Title: The Lion King
fields.Caption: Cast members with Michelle Obama at the White House
